subject: [PATCH 0/3] block: skip the blkcg walk in blk_cgroup_congested() when nothing is throttled

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author responded to Tejun Heo's feedback that pd->blkg is only set when the pd is attached to a blkg, and explained that the pd never had ->blkg assigned in the GFP_NOWAIT allocation failure case, so it reads as NULL rather than garbage.
reviews.raw_body:
Not in the normal case.

pd->blkg is only set when the pd is attached to a blkg.
blkcg_activate_policy() pre-allocates one outside the queue_lock when the
GFP_NOWAIT allocation fails, and frees it through pd_free_fn() if it ends up
unused \u2014 both at the retry and at the out: label. That pd never had ->blkg assigned.
It reads as NULL rather than garbage because iolatency_pd_alloc() uses kzalloc_node().

Good to keep as a guard in this case?

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged the need for revisions to address Tejun Heo's feedback and agreed to restructure in a new version (v2) of the patch.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks! Ack on all 3. I will wait a day incase there are more comments
and send a new revision tomorrow with all 3 addressed.

2026-08-12.patch_summary: This patch set optimizes the blk_cgroup_congested() function by skipping unnecessary walks of the block cgroup (blkcg) hierarchy when no tasks are being throttled. The current implementation incurs a significant performance cost due to frequent cache line loads and RCU read-side pairs, especially in systems with deep container hierarchies. To address this, the patch introduces a global gate that only performs the walk when there is at least one blkcg with a non-zero congestion count. Additionally, two patches fix issues that can leave a blkcg permanently marked congested, which would otherwise cause unnecessary throttling of tasks in affected cgroups.
